tagline: Record a personal video message with a unique tracked link per recipient
verdictSummary: Recording a quick personal video message and tracking whether a specific recipient actually watched it — Vidyard's actual sales-outreach angle — is a real weekend build using standard browser video recording and view-tracking. What doesn't survive: Vidyard's video hosting at scale, its CRM integrations, and analytics on exactly how much of the video each viewer watched.
coreLoopDIY: Record a short video message in the browser using the MediaRecorder API, generate a unique shareable link per recipient, and track whether that specific link was opened and the video played.
whatYouLose: hosted video infrastructure and CDN delivery at scale
personalized video thumbnails with the recipient's name overlaid
whyPeopleStillPay: Recording and hosting one video is simple; delivering video reliably at scale, integrating with the CRM tools sales teams live in, and showing exactly how far each of hundreds of recipients watched, is the ongoing infrastructure work.
prompt: Build a personal video-messaging tool for sales-style outreach: record a quick video in the browser, generate a unique link per recipient, and track whether they watched it. Use a browser-based recorder, the MediaRecorder API, to capture webcam and/or screen video directly in the browser, upload it to your own storage, local disk or S3-compatible, on stop. Generate a unique shareable link per send, not just per video, since the same video can be sent to multiple recipients each getting their own tracked link, using a UUID. When a recipient opens their link, record a 'viewed' timestamp, and use the video player's timeupdate event to track roughly how much of the video played, a simple percentage, not frame-accurate analytics. Show the sender a dashboard of sends with viewed/not-viewed status and rough watch percentage. Do not build CDN-scale video delivery, CRM integrations, or personalized thumbnail generation — those are out of scope; this is a personal tool for sending a handful of tracked video messages, not infrastructure for a sales team's volume. Requires hosting, storage for video files, and a domain for the tracked links; no other external service needed.

faq.q: Can I send the same video to multiple people and track each separately?
faq.a: Yes — each send gets its own unique link, so you can tell exactly which recipient watched, even though the underlying video file is shared.

faq.q: How accurate is the watch-time tracking?
faq.a: Rough — a simple percentage based on the video player's playback position, not Vidyard's more granular per-second analytics.

faq.q: Will it handle sending videos to hundreds of prospects?
faq.a: Not well — this is scoped as a personal tool for a handful of tracked sends, not infrastructure built for a sales team's volume. Video storage and delivery at scale is real infrastructure work.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting, video storage, and a domain — costs scale with how much video you store and how many people watch it, but stay modest at personal scale.
